correct_answer: No — the CFO's emoji reaction is not a formal approval, the CFO declined the review meeting, Legal has not responded, and the approval matrix v2 Section 2.4 requires all three approvals plus Legal review
rationale: The current approval matrix (v2, effective Jan 2025) Section 2.4 explicitly requires four approvals for adding a new brand to an existing multi-brand operator: Brand VP, Franchise Operations Director, CFO, and Legal review. The CFO office's thumbs-up emoji on a Slack message is not a formal approval — it is an acknowledgment at best, and critically, the CFO declined the Franchise Expansion Review calendar meeting, meaning no substantive CFO review occurred. Legal has neither responded to the email nor attended any meeting. The DocuSign envelope is missing both CFO and Legal signers, confirming these approvals are outstanding. Answer D incorrectly treats a Slack emoji as formal CFO approval and ignores the missing Legal review entirely. Answer C applies a superseded policy version — v1 was replaced in January 2025 and the new brand addition is happening in 2026; there is no grandfathering provision for approval processes (unlike operational standards). Answer D partially identifies the gap but incorrectly accepts the emoji as CFO approval; the declined calendar invite is the critical hidden signal proving the CFO has NOT engaged substantively with this decision.
